newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN TO OFFER NEW PROPOSALS TO HUN SEN.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN TO OFFER NEW PROPOSALS TO HUN SEN.

text.p: The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) will offer fresh proposals to Cambodian strongman Hun Sen in an attempt to mediate in the conflict in his country, Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Wednesday.
Speaking to reporters after talks Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot, Alatas did not give details about the proposals.
But he said: "We assessed that the situation in Cambodia has not changed to such an extent which warrants us to change our decision (not to accept Cambodia into Asean now)."
ASEAN foreign ministers earlier reaffirmed a decision to postpone the admission of Cambodia into the grouping, while formally accepting Burma and Laos as members.
But ASEAN did accept an offer by Ung Huot to mediate in the Cambodian crisis that erupted when Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"We told him (Ung Huot) that there are still unresolved issues in the state and also there is the question of a new prime minister to be appointed by the end of the month," Alatas said.

Alatas said he and two other members of an ASEAN delegation -- Thai Foreign Minister Prachaub Chaiyasan and Filipino Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon -- asked Ung Huot to convey ASEAN's proposals to Hun Sen.
The three foreign ministers met Hun Sen last weekend when he rejected their offer of mediation, but he has apparently had a change of heart since then.

Alatas said it was still "too premature" to predict Hun Sen's reaction to the proposals but added: "We hope to make progress and of course, as quickly as possible, as time is running out. I don't know how they will respond."
